name: District of Columbia
$methodComment: Genuinely the SIMPLEST bracket shape in this project structurally, despite DC's real-world reputation for a steep top rate (10.75%): ONE bracket table for every filing status (like Rhode Island), and the ONLY reduction is a flat per-ALLOWANCE dollar amount subtracted BEFORE the bracket lookup -- no separate standard deduction line at all in the withholding formula (unlike the RETURN-level DC-1040, which does have a large standard deduction; several secondary sources conflated the two, the same withholding-formula-vs-return-level distinction already caught for California/Utah/Colorado in this project). D-4's own allowance count folds self/HOH/age/blind/spouse/dependents into ONE number, all valued identically at the same per-allowance dollar figure -- unlike DC's own field name ('Dependent Allowance = $X x Number of Dependents' in NFC's formula), the count is NOT literally dependents-only; it's the FULL D-4 Line total.

sources.title: NFC-22-1668460546, District of Columbia Income Tax Withholding (USDA National Finance Center bulletin, effective Pay Period 22, 2022)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly -- the fullest primary-adjacent source found this session for DC's actual WITHHOLDING formula (DC's own OTR did not have a current-year FR-230 booklet locatable this session; only pre-2018 archived versions were found via search). The bracket thresholds and rates ($0-$10k @4%, $10k-$40k @6%, $40k-$60k @6.5%, $60k-$250k @8.5%, $250k-$500k @9.25%, $500k-$1M @9.75%, $1M+ @10.75%) were cross-checked against MULTIPLE independent 2026-dated secondary sources and found to match EXACTLY -- strong evidence DC's brackets have been stable since 2022 and this formula is still current, though the allowance dollar amount specifically (see below) carries a real, disclosed staleness risk this cross-check does not resolve.

sources.title: D-4, DC Employee Withholding Allowance Certificate instructions (secondary confirmation of the allowance-counting mechanism)
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed. Quoted: 'Total allowances are calculated by summing yourself, head of household status, age/blind allowances, spouse, and dependent allowances' -- confirms the NFC formula's 'Dependent Allowance = $X x Number of Dependents' label is really 'per-allowance amount x TOTAL D-4 allowance count,' not literally dependents-only, resolving what would otherwise look like a contradiction between the two sources.

sources.title: D.C. Code § 1-206.02(a)(5) (Home Rule Act § 602(a)(5)) nonresident-taxation prohibition
sources.verifiedBy: Primary text read 2026-10-18 (D.C. Code § 1-206.02(a)(5): the Council may not '(5) Impose any tax on the whole or any portion of the personal income, either directly or at the source thereof, of any individual not a resident of the District'); the earlier citation to § 47-1806.04 was wrong (that section covers credits). Earlier cross_source_confirmed across multiple sources (a state-and-local-tax law blog, a fiscal policy institute analysis) agreeing: 'The federal 1973 Home Rule Act gave the District the power to levy taxes, including income taxes, but it barred the District from taxing the personal income of nonresidents.' A genuinely different, BROADER mechanism than reciprocity as modelled anywhere else in this project -- not a bilateral agreement with 2-4 named states, but a blanket federal-statutory prohibition applying to residents of ALL 50 states equally.

sources.title: DC Universal Paid Leave (UPL) 0.75% employer-only rate
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed. Genuinely different shape from every other paid-leave program in this project: 100% EMPLOYER-funded, zero employee share -- Washington/Colorado/Oregon/New Jersey/Connecticut/New York's own paid-leave programs in this project all have at least some employee contribution; DC's has none.

bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.bracketsComment: Verbatim from the NFC formula, and internally chain-verified before trusting it: 400 + (40000-10000)x0.06=400+1800=2200 (matches); 2200+(60000-40000)x0.065=2200+1300=3500 (matches); 3500+(250000-60000)x0.085=3500+16150=19650 (matches); 19650+(500000-250000)x0.0925=19650+23125=42775 (matches); 42775+(1000000-500000)x0.0975=42775+48750=91525 (matches) -- every published base independently reproduced from the one before it, zero discrepancies. ONE table for all filing statuses.
bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.allowanceAmountComment: CONFIRMED 2026-10-18: OTR Tax Notice 2022-08 (Oct 17, 2022, https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/release/otr-tax-notice-2022-08-district-columbia-withholding-tax-year-2022) tells employers to withhold using the 2022 rate schedule 'and the federal allowance amount for tax year 2022', because the TCJA suspension of personal exemptions left OTR unable to produce its own tables. The federal allowance amount is $4,300: IRS Pub 15-T (2026), Worksheet 1A line 1k, 'Multiply line 1j by $4,300' (also the NFC TAXES 22-28 change from $4,150). OTR has published no FR-230 since 2018 (that edition used $4,150) and its D-4 is 'currently under review', so $4,300 follows from OTR's own rule plus the IRS figure rather than from a printed OTR number. An aggregator page showing $4,150 repeats the 2018 value.
bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.noCertificateDefault: Zero allowances, no standard deduction. OTR FR-230 (2018, the last edition OTR printed): 'If a DC RESIDENT EMPLOYEE fails to furnish a certificate, the employer is required to withhold DC income tax as if the employee had not claimed any withholding allowances.' Also: 'The standard deduction will not be used in the withholding calculation.' (https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/otr/publication/attachments/2018%20FR-230_12.13.17.pdf)

pretaxVerification.result: D.C. Code 47-1801.04: 'Wages' means wages as defined in IRC 3401(a). OTR's FR-230 (2018) names no pre-tax category; federal conformity.
pretaxVerification.outcome: No source contradicts any category in exemptPretax; categories not individually named rest on federal conformity.

exemptComment: DC's withholding formula itself is built on federal AGI-adjacent wages (subtract TSP/401k-style deferrals and pretax health benefits BEFORE annualizing, per the NFC formula's own Steps 1-3) -- the clearest, most directly-sourced exemptPretax basis of any state in this project except Arizona's A-4/Michigan's RAB-1988-27, since the WITHHOLDING FORMULA ITSELF spells out the subtraction steps rather than requiring an inference from a general AGI-conformity statute.

reciprocity.rule: STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from reciprocity everywhere else in this project: DC does not tax NONRESIDENT wages AT ALL, for residents of any of the 50 states, under a blanket federal prohibition (the 1973 Home Rule Act), not a bilateral agreement with specific named states. certificate.nonresident (a boolean, not a reciprocalStates list lookup) should zero DC withholding entirely for any employee who does not reside in DC, regardless of which state they DO reside in.
reciprocity.notModelledAsReciprocalStatesList: Deliberately NOT using this project's generic reciprocityExemptionReason()/reciprocalStates mechanism, because that mechanism checks residenceState.code against a closed LIST of specific states -- DC's actual rule is unconditional across all 50 states, which a finite list would have to (redundantly, and riskily forgettably) enumerate one by one. A dedicated nonresident check is the correct, not just convenient, way to model this specific fact.

localIncomeTax.rule: N/A -- DC has no sub-jurisdictions (no counties, no cities within DC) to levy a SEPARATE local tax; the DC income tax modelled above already IS the whole story, the same way NH/WA/etc.'s 'no income tax' entries are complete in themselves.

universalPaidLeave.$comment: DC Universal Paid Leave — 100% employer-funded, genuinely the only paid-leave program in this project with ZERO employee contribution. Computed as DC_PFML_ER via the statePaidLeaveEmployer block below — employerSizeGated:false, since DC's programme has no headcount threshold and every covered employer owes it.

unemploymentInsurance.$comment: Employer-only (SUI) -- no employee contribution. NOT researched this session -- no figures recorded rather than guessed.
unemploymentInsurance.confidence: NOT VERIFIED this session — a genuine, disclosed gap, not silently skipped.

verification: PROVEN via calculatePaycheck(): the bracket table's own internal base-chain was independently verified (see bracketsComment) before being used to hand-derive test fixtures, since no full worked example with a stated final dollar answer was found in the NFC bulletin the way California/Rhode Island's own sources provided. See tests/engine.test.ts, describe('District of Columbia').
knownGaps: RESOLVED 2026-10-18: the $4,300 allowance follows OTR Tax Notice 2022-08 ('the federal allowance amount') and IRS Pub 15-T (2026) Worksheet 1A line 1k; see allowanceAmountComment. It is derived from OTR's rule, not a number OTR prints; if OTR ever publishes a 2026+ FR-230 or a new D-4, compare.

No current-year (2026) FR-230 booklet was locatable from DC's own OTR site this session -- this file rests on a federal-payroll-oriented secondary-primary source (NFC) rather than DC's own primary withholding publication.

STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.
Universal Paid Leave (0.75%, employer-only) is computed as DC_PFML_ER via the statePaidLeaveEmployer block — see universalPaidLeave.$comment above.
The no-certificate default (zero allowances) is stated in OTR's 2018 FR-230; see bracketAnnualAllowanceDeduction.noCertificateDefault.

Supplemental wages: DC's own FR-230 Employer Withholding Instructions were checked directly (2018 revision, the most recent full booklet publicly available, cross-checked against the NFC bulletin already cited in this file for anything current-year might have added) -- neither contains a distinct supplemental-wage withholding procedure at all, only a general definition of taxable "wages" that happens to name bonuses as an example. Third-party guides describing a DC supplemental rate are actually describing the FEDERAL 22%/37% flat rate, not a DC-specific one. A standalone bonus therefore runs through the same formula as any other wages, which is what this engine already does by default -- the same conclusion reached for South Carolina, Utah, and Arkansas in this project, each checked directly rather than assumed.

CHECKED 2026-10-01: the FY2027 Budget Support (Emergency) Act cuts Universal Paid Leave BENEFITS for claims filed on or after 2026-10-01 (family leave 12 -> 6 weeks, medical 12 -> 10 weeks, weekly cap $1,190 -> $1,100) but leaves the employer contribution at 0.75% of covered wages with no employee contribution, so DC_PFML_ER is unchanged (Epstein Becker Green, 2026-09-23; secondary source, permanent act still in congressional review to about 2026-11-20). This engine computes the contribution, not benefits.

suiVerification.result: UI $9,000; new employer 'average rate... or 2.7 percent, whichever is higher'; UPL 0.75% employer-paid for every 2026 quarter.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: 2026 taxable wage bases cross-checked against EY's published 2026 state-by-state table; where this file already carried a numeric wage base, the two agreed unless noted in wageBaseNote.
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: DC's 2026 unemployment rate announcement: the new-employer rate remains 2.7% on a $9,000 wage base, alongside a separate 0.2% administrative assessment that this engine does not add (it is an assessment, not the contribution rate, and is disclosed here rather than folded in).

statePaidLeaveEmployer.$comment: DC Universal Paid Leave, wired from this file's own universalPaidLeave block: 0.75% of covered wages, funded 100% by the employer — the only paid-leave programme in this project with ZERO employee contribution. employerSizeGated is false because DC's programme has no headcount threshold at all: every covered employer owes it, so requiring a caller to assert liability first would just suppress a tax that is always due. No wage cap.
